summary: A federal judge in Mississippi sanctioned all four lawyers on both sides of a civil case after filings cited fake legal cases linked to unverified AI use. All four were removed from the case and fined, and two were barred for two years.
technical_summary: AI drafting and research tools produced fabricated case citations that lawyers on both sides placed in court filings without checking them. The attorneys acknowledged at a hearing that they had not verified the authenticity of the cases. The court found violations of the rule requiring a reasonable inquiry before filing.

OpenAI said the questions followed a factual line that would not trigger self-harm safeguards. The AI role was information retrieval, with harm caused by the user's deliberate acts.

summary: An Ontario court found a lawyer's filing cited cases that were irrelevant, misrepresented or did not exist and asked whether generative AI had been used. The judge ordered the lawyer to show cause why she should not be held in contempt.
technical_summary: A court factum contained links to cases that did not support the stated propositions or led to error pages, a pattern consistent with generative AI fabricating or misattributing citations. The citations were caught by the judge at the hearing rather than by the filer's own review.

summary: RealPage's YieldStar software recommends rents to landlords using data including competitors' private pricing. Reports and lawsuits allege it pushed rents up and reduced competition across many US markets, which the company's own executives credited with driving large rent increases.
technical_summary: A pricing algorithm pools nonpublic rent and occupancy data from competing landlords to recommend daily prices, with a high share of recommendations reportedly accepted. This is alleged to coordinate prices, discourage negotiation and reduce vacancies in favor of higher rents, prompting private and federal antitrust suits.
